noise_why: K15.30's noise, unchanged, and it applies here: the rule is the same (routing-quality.md's totals rule for a change to profile enhanced: accept when the total improves by more than the set's noise, sqrt(sum of the per-board bands squared)) and so are the rows, the boards and the input. canary-pwr's band is its registered 10 (docs/roadmap/prereg/K09.json `noise.canary-pwr`, N02's variant spread, as K14.json, K15.14 and K15.30), a constant of the rule and not a property of this engine. script.what: K13.5's version, unchanged (K13.json and K14.json pin the same hash): per router call ulimit -v ROUTE_MEMORY_KB and timeout -k 10 ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S; the plugin's own export or snapshot and import; grading as tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh --keep-tracks under the project's own .kicad_pro/.kicad_dru with the copper classes forced to error, `kicad-cli pcb drc --severity-all --refill-zones` on the input and the routed board, routing-caused items on Q22.2's copper basis; SHARE_GRADE_WITH copies the grade of a byte-identical session

helper.what: K15.14's helper, unchanged (the same sha256 as K15.14's `helper`): `prepare` (the boards, from `boards`), `run` (the registration's `commands`, verbatim) and `collect` (records.json for the gate and table.md, from the arms each row's `commands` lists and the registered `metrics`); nothing in it names K15.14's flag or arms. `collect` also computes K15.13's pour-guard count, which is not a registered metric here and so is not recorded; table.md's 'pours guarded' column is 0 in every arm and is not read

grading: per row, pcb-off then pcb-on; pcb-on with SHARE_GRADE_WITH its pcb-off arm, so a session byte-identical to the baseline's copies its grade (summary grade_shared_with). Under the board's own rules (rules = project: the row's .kicad_pro and .kicad_dru, hashed in rules_files), the same oracle, metrics and manufacturing types as K13.6, K14.6 and K15.14. kicad-cli only while `pgrep -x kicad-cli` shows none, one job at a time, no other heavy run at the same time
limits: K15.30's: every router call (the load check and the route) under ulimit -v 8000000 (ROUTE_MEMORY_KB) and timeout -k 10 300 (ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S); every route with `--max-passes 2 --timeout 240` after the plugin's flags. A call that hits ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S or is killed by a signal (exit status 124 or above) is aborted = 1 and not graded. A route the router's own --timeout stopped (result manifest final_state TIMED_OUT) depends on the machine's speed, so its row is not judged (validity (b)). The pair costs route time (K15.31: contacts are recomputed per pour as the board changes): seen on main c4f74fb in the orchestrator's check (target/orchestrator/k1537pre/runs, release) pcu-76163c7 162.5 s -> 191.6 s (+18 %) and canary-pwr-95882f00 93.1 s -> 159.8 s (+72 %); K15.31 saw 163 s -> 176 s and 92 s -> 153 s. Both stay under the 240 s deadline, so the K15.30 caps are kept. A row near the deadline without the pair is at risk of timing out with it: kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 took 171.1 s in K15.30's pcb-off arm and would reach 240 s at +40 %; loratracker-hardware-loratracker-hat 57 s, moteus-moteus-c1 65 s and pcie-active-backplane 41 s are far below. The registered handling is validity (b) (such a row is left out of the judgement) plus guard (4) (its time counts), not a longer deadline. Estimated time: 34 calls. K15.30's run took 34 min for its 34 calls (2026-10-22 04:14 to 04:48): 673.7 s of routing in pcb-off and 706.1 s in pcb-on over its 16 judged rows, pocketsdr-v3-0 2 x 240 s, and the rest the plugin's snapshot, import and kicad-cli grading. With the pair: about +30 s on pcu, +67 s on canary-pwr, and up to +72 % on the other judged rows' 420 s (+300 s), plus the grading of every pcb-on session that now differs from pcb-off's (K15.30 shared the grade of the rows that did not change). Expected: about 40-55 min; the bound if every call hit ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S is 34 x about 330 s = 3.1 h

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: summary via_in_pad: tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py's vias_in_pads on the routed board minus the input board's, floored at 0 (D8)
metric_definitions.below_minimum: summary below_minimum: routed tracks and vias (whose nanometre copper key the input board does not have) under the Board Setup minimum track width, via diameter or via drill, summed
metric_definitions.manufacturing_breaches: summary manufacturing_breaches: the routing-caused KiCad DRC items (Q22.2's copper basis) of the types clearance, hole_clearance, hole_to_hole, copper_edge_clearance, track_width, via_diameter, annular_width, drill_out_of_range, solder_mask_bridge, shorting_items, summed
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: the signal: summary unconnected, kicad-cli's unconnected_items on the routed board after --refill-zones
metric_definitions.zone_zone_unconnected: secondary: the routed board's unconnected items (routed/drc.json, or the shared grade's) whose items are all zones: a pour split into islands that KiCad cannot join (K15.13's count)
metric_definitions.zone_zone_zones: the distinct (net, layer) zones those items name
metric_definitions.router_incomplete: the router's own incomplete connections at the end: the result manifest's board_statistics.connections.incomplete_count (work/<name>.result.json)
metric_definitions.kicad_less_router: secondary: kicad_unconnected - router_incomplete, how far KiCad's count is above the router's (K15.25 on pcu-76163c7: 36 off and 35 on; on canary-pwr-95882f00: 13 and 12)
metric_definitions.drc_real: guard (2): the sum of summary routing_caused_by_type (the grader's drc_real), every type
metric_definitions.route_seconds: guard (4): summary route_s, the routing call's wall-clock seconds
metric_definitions.connections: the result manifest's board_statistics.connections.maximum_count: the board's connections as the router loaded it, the default noise band's base
metric_definitions.input_unconnected: summary input_unconnected: kicad-cli's unconnected_items on the stripped input board

validity: checked before keep_rule, per row: (a) both settings reached the router: each pcb-on arm's result manifest (OUT/<row>/pcb-on/work/<stem>.result.json) has settings_snapshot.pour_fill_target true and settings_snapshot.pour_fill_contacts true, and no pcb-off arm's has either true (unset, so absent); a row whose pcb-on session is byte-identical to pcb-off's (summary grade_shared_with set) is judged as it is (the settings changed no route there) and named; (b) the row is judged when both its arms have aborted 0, graded true and final_state COMPLETED; a row COMPLETED in pcb-off and TIMED_OUT in pcb-on (the pair needs more than the registered 240 s router deadline) is left out by (b) like any other, its pcb-on result depending on the machine's speed, but it is named with both route times and guard (4) counts it; (c) amendment 1 is written before the first arm and `cargo test -p freerouting-dev --test prereg_k15_37` passes in TREE. A row that fails (a) or (b), or whose board is missing, is left out of the judgement and reported by name with its reason; the keep rule, guards (2) and (3) and the set noise are then over the judged rows only (guard (4) as it says). The measurement is 'not measured' (decision_table) only when fewer than min_boards (3) distinct rows are judged, pcu-76163c7 or canary-pwr-95882f00 is not judged (must_judge), or (c) fails
guards: (1) in every arm that runs and is graded, judged row or not: manufacturing_breaches = 0, below_minimum = 0 and via_in_pad = 0, absolutely (decided 2026-10-20: routing never breaks the board's manufacturing rules; routing-quality.md, order of importance items 1 and 2); the gate's HARD lines of the verdict pair and the reported pair, and summary.json for the rows left out. (2) routing-caused DRC not up: the sum of drc_real over the judged rows in pcb-on is at most pcb-off's. (3) no row worse than its own noise band (K15.14's guard, decided 2026-10-21): on every judged row, pcb-on's kicad_unconnected is at most pcb-off's + the row's band, the totals rule's per-row band (canary-pwr-95882f00 10, every other row max(2, ceil(5 % of its connections)), noise_why). (4) route time: the sum of route_seconds in pcb-on over the judged rows and over every row COMPLETED in pcb-off and TIMED_OUT in pcb-on (validity (b); its pcb-on value is the deadline, about 240.1 s, a lower bound of its time) is at most 1.25 x the sum of pcb-off's over the same rows
keep_rule: kept when validity holds (at least 3 distinct rows judged, pcu-76163c7 and canary-pwr-95882f00 among them, (c)), guard (1) holds, the signal improves (S: the sum of pcb-on's kicad_unconnected over the judged rows is lower than pcb-off's by more than the set noise sqrt(sum of the bands squared), noise_why; strictly more, as the gate computes it) and guards (2), (3) and (4) hold
keep_rule_by_hand: from OUT/records.json and OUT/table.md (`python3 -I TREE/tools/bench/k15_all_pours.py collect TREE/docs/roadmap/prereg/K15.37.json OUT`) and the gate (TREE's freerouting-dev, the commands of heavy_run's last step, with --prereg ROOT's docs/roadmap/prereg/K15.37.json as amended): `gate ... --baseline OUT/baseline.json --write-baseline`, then `gate ... --baseline OUT/baseline.json --all-pairs`, each with `--left-out ROW=REASON` for every row validity (b) leaves out (K15.21). The verdict pair's 'totals verdict' line is S, with the set noise it prints; its HARD lines and the reported pair's are guard (1); guards (2)-(4) are summed by hand from records.json (guard (4) with the rows validity (b) names); validity (a) from the result manifests and (b) from table.md's state column. The reverse pair is there for its HARD lines only; its totals verdict is the verdict pair's mirror and is not read

decision_table.not measured: fewer than min_boards (3) distinct rows judged, pcu-76163c7 or canary-pwr-95882f00 not judged, or validity (c) fails (a row left out by validity (a) or (b) does not by itself make the measurement 'not measured': it is reported by name and the other rows are judged): K15.37 stays [~] naming the rows and reasons; nothing changes in the product; the rows are run again only after the cause is fixed (a longer timeout_s or a fix), under an amendment naming it, with nothing else changed
decision_table.breach: the measurement is not 'not measured' and guard (1) fails in any graded arm (of a judged row or not): K15.37 stays [~] naming the arm, row and items; the breach is fixed in an item of its own (a pcb-on breach that pcb-off lacks is a defect of the pair; one in pcb-off is a defect of today's default), then the registered run repeats at the fixed commit under an amendment; until then `router.pour_fill_contacts` and `router.pour_fill_target` stay opt-in, unset in both profiles, and the plugin does not offer `router.pour_fill_contacts` (K15.30's `pour_fill_target` option, already offered, stays) (decided 2026-10-20: fix gains, don't remove them; never ship below-minimum copper)
decision_table.not kept, guard: none of the above, S holds and any of guards (2), (3), (4) fails over the judged rows: both settings stay opt-in, unset in both profiles, and the plugin offers `router.pour_fill_contacts` as an option beside K15.30's `pour_fill_target` one (the options.py field, the dialog's checkbox and plugin tests, as 'not kept, no gain'); K15.37's note names the failing guard and its rows, and a follow-up item may fix the cost and measure again under a new registration (fix gains, don't remove them)
decision_table.not kept, no gain: neither of the above, and S fails over the judged rows: both settings stay opt-in, unset in both profiles; the plugin offers `router.pour_fill_contacts` as an option beside K15.30's `pour_fill_target` one (an options.py RouteOptions field `pour_fill_contacts`, off in both profiles, whose to_args adds `--router.pour_fill_contacts=true` only when on; from_dict and from_form; a checkbox on the Advanced tab's Flow group below K15.30's, whose tooltip says it is meant to be used with 'End traces where KiCad fills a pour' (the setting alone counts the open islands but does not route them, K15.31) and gives this measurement's totals and the two owner boards' numbers without private board names; plugin tests, as K15.30 did for `pour_fill_target`); K15.37's note records the table; DIVERGENCES' `pour_fill_contacts` and `pour_fill_target` entries (board model) and the 'Not in `enhanced`' docs of board/pour_contacts.rs and autoroute/pour_target.rs get the numbers
decision_table.kept: none of the above: validity, guard (1), S and guards (2), (3), (4) all hold over the judged rows: `router.pour_fill_contacts` and `router.pour_fill_target` both join the ENHANCED table (crates/freerouting/src/settings/profile.rs) as true, in one change (they are measured as a pair; contacts alone is worse than unset on pcu, K15.31); tests/settings_defaults.rs pins enhanced's true for both and legacy's unset; DIVERGENCES' 'Profile `enhanced`' section gets a line per setting with this measurement's totals, and its board-model entries and the 'Not in `enhanced`' docs of autoroute/pour_target.rs and board/pour_contacts.rs say they are enhanced's; `legacy` unchanged: `PARITY_SET=tools/bench/sets/connection-parity.txt tools/parity-check.sh --no-probes` 7 of 7 exact; the plugin's option for `pour_fill_target` (K15.30: RouteOptions.pour_fill_target, its checkbox, from_dict and from_form, their tests) is removed, because with the profile carrying the setting the field would add a flag that is already set and could not switch it off (a user who wants Java's rules picks profile legacy), and a stored `pour_fill_target` key in an options file is ignored (schema 6 stays); the plugin passes nothing for `pour_fill_contacts` (the profile carries it)
decision_table.order: the rows are tried in the order not measured, breach, not kept no gain, not kept guard, kept; the first whose condition holds decides, so every outcome maps to exactly one row

report: per row and arm: kicad_unconnected (input_unconnected), zone_zone_unconnected and zone_zone_zones, router_incomplete and kicad_less_router, manufacturing_breaches, below_minimum, via_in_pad, routing_caused_by_type and drc_real, route_seconds, final_state, settings_snapshot.pour_fill_target and settings_snapshot.pour_fill_contacts, board_statistics.connections.maximum_count, aborted, session_sha256 and whether the grade is shared; the rows left out of the judgement and why (a row COMPLETED in pcb-off and TIMED_OUT in pcb-on with both route times); the totals over the judged rows, the set noise and every band; for pcu-76163c7 and canary-pwr-95882f00 the comparison with the numbers in seen_before_registration
known_effects: with both settings the router's incomplete count is within 1 of KiCad's unconnected on the seen boards (pcu 21 and 22, canary-pwr 26 and 27 at K15.36; without them 11 against 47 and 27 against 40): the router counts a pad the fill does not reach as open and, with the target, routes the islands together (K15.31). It costs route time (limits). Alone, `pour_fill_contacts` counts the open islands but does not route them (pcu 48, canary-pwr 38 at K15.31), which is why only the pair is measured. The seen gains are pcu 47 -> 20 (-27) and canary-pwr 40 -> 26 (-14), 41 together, against a set noise of about 67 over 16 rows: S holds only if the other 14 judged rows gain 27 more between them, and K15.30's run moved those rows by 0 to 2 each with the target alone (the nine unchanged rows summed to 114 in both arms), so 'not kept, no gain' is the likely outcome unless contacts move other boards; the table is registered as the repository's keep rule has it (routing-quality.md), with the seen owner-board gains recorded for the plugin option the outcome then adds. The router's own pour contacts stay Java's in pcb-off, and K15.38 moved `pour_fill_target` alone on pcu from 49 to 51 (the NPTH cut moves that route), so K15.30's target-alone numbers are not this baseline. Both arms import the session whole, as the plugin does (fix_existing off), on stripped boards with no input copper. pocketsdr-v3-0 hit the 240 s deadline in both arms of K15.30 and may again; kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 (171 s in K15.30's pcb-off) may time out in pcb-on (limits)
